also_verified_on: 1.0.1-R2006.1, 1.1.0-R2009.1, 1.1.0-R2074.1 (39 entries on every build; only the /effort hint differs — its row)
count_semantics: DISCREPANCY (resolved per later report): host-reality.md / canary-diff.md / 00-DECISION.md count 39 'built-in slash commands'. That 39 is the row count of the default composer picker on a pristine HOME (tui-slash-theme §1.4, canary-diff §1): 31 built-in TUI commands + 7 bundled-skill shortcuts + the bundled `loop` plugin command. The binary's own built-in slash table (rodata literal at 0xb806baf) holds 36 canonical commands + 9 aliases (tui-slash-theme verification R1 corrected the report's '37 + 10'; cli-surface §5 called 36 'a floor'; 00-SYNTHESIS §10.2 resolves it to 36 + 9). Six built-ins are hidden from browsing but resolvable by prefix or unlocked by a provider/gate. `items` below is the 39 per host-reality, each tagged with `kind`; `hidden_builtins` carries the rest so the collision set is complete.

field_semantics.name: the spelling shown as this picker row (canary-diff list)
field_semantics.canonical: the canonical name in the binary slash table (differs from name only for the /quit row)
field_semantics.aliases: alias spellings from the binary table that resolve to this canonical — never a canonical name itself; the union over items + hidden_builtins is exactly the 9 builtin_aliases
field_semantics.kind: builtin | bundled-skill-shortcut | bundled-plugin-command | builtin-plugin-skill (the second builtin plugin's skill row, since 1.3.0-R3057.1)

capture_method: pty harness with a pristine HOME, --provider echo, workspace trusted, no gates; stepping the picker with the down arrow (canary-diff §1; tui-slash-theme §1.4). The picker reflects installed plugins, so any baseline must be taken against a clean profile.

items.name: /create-skill
items.description: Create and validate a new Muse skill — project-local in the current workspace by default, or a personal skill staged for `muse skills install` into the managed personal root. Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks to create a Muse skill or invokes the create-skill skill. Do NOT use for ordinary skill usage, code changes, benchmark tasks, or third-party skill/plugin systems.

items.name: /doctor
items.description: Diagnose Muse Code product/runtime issues from installed binary evidence. Use ONLY when the user explicitly invokes the doctor skill, asks to debug/troubleshoot Muse Code itself, asks what happened earlier in the current Muse Code session, or explicitly selects an earlier Muse Code session. Do NOT use for ordinary repository code failures or history, benchmark tasks, implementation debugging, build/test hangs, or third-party project issues.

items.name: /grill
items.description: Run a decision-forcing interview only when the user explicitly asks to be grilled, pressure-tested, or stress-tested.

items.name: /import
items.description: Import a Claude Code, Codex, or Grok session
items.note: Picker/help shows the skill's metadata.short-description; the full description is 'Resume a third-party coding-agent session from a local transcript, path, or session id.'

items.name: /manage-settings
items.description: Any explicit Muse Code setting question or change (model, reasoning effort, /settings) requires a silent read_skill call for bundled:manage-settings as FIRST ACTION—no assistant text or other tool first. Never use for repository, app, eval, or other non-Muse configuration.

items.name: /migrate
items.description: Bring what Claude Code or Codex already remembers or has configured for this user into Muse Code — their memory notes and their MCP servers — whenever the user mentions things Claude Code or Codex remembers or knows about them, an MCP tool or server they had there that is missing here, or asks to migrate, import, or copy that setup; call read_skill for bundled:migrate before reading any foreign file. Rules and skills are already covered by /rules import and `muse skills import --from claude|codex`; point there. Do NOT use for session transcripts (resume-claude or resume-codex for Claude Code/Codex continuation, including recovery of unfinished work with or without a handle; import for explicit /import requests or continuation from other agents or unnamed artifacts), for Muse settings unrelated to migration (manage-settings), or when Claude Code or Codex is only mentioned in passing.

items.name: /plan
items.description: Create a grounded, decision-complete plan, then stop for approval. Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks to plan — when they request a plan, design, approach, rollout/migration strategy, or PR breakdown, or invoke the plan skill (/skill plan). Do NOT use for ordinary implement, build, fix, debug, or refactor requests — when asked to make a code change, implement it directly without planning first. One rule applies whether or not you read the body: when an explicit plan divides work into separate diffs, commits, or PRs and you are asked to publish, publish that split — never silently collapse the planned units into fewer; tell the user before deviating.

items.name: /resume-claude
items.description: Continue work from a local Claude Code session in Muse Code. Use when the user asks to resume, continue, or recover unfinished Claude Code work, with or without a session ID or log path; call read_skill for bundled:resume-claude before reading its transcript. Explicit /import requests use import.

items.name: /resume-codex
items.description: Continue work from a local Codex session in Muse Code. Use when the user asks to resume, continue, or recover unfinished Codex work, with or without a session ID or log path; call read_skill for bundled:resume-codex before reading its transcript. Explicit /import requests use import.

telemetry_vocabulary.note: tbh_agent::command_invoked::BUILTIN_SLASH_COMMAND_NAMES — a 37-entry &[&str] in __DATA_CONST (36 canonical + the alias /quit as its own entry). Plugin commands and skill shortcuts are reported as the literal `custom`. Nothing is demonstrably dropped (tui-slash-theme verification R2 refuted the earlier TELEMETRY_DROPPED inference).

notes: Plugin commands (capabilities.commands[], commands/<id>.md with `description` + `argument-hint` front matter and $ARGUMENTS substitution) are appended to this picker and to /help → Custom commands; they do NOT need MUSE_EXPERIMENTAL_PLUGINS at run time.
A server-pushed `killed_slash_commands` list (feature-config cache, next to `gates`) can remove commands; TBH_UNKILL_SLASH_COMMANDS is the local escape hatch. Empty in the offline build.
Rebinding tui.keymap.app.commands away from `/` drops the 7 bundled-skill shortcuts and /loop from the picker (39 rows → 31).
The slash drawer shows 7 rows at a time plus a `↓ N more` footer (7 + 32 = 39).
